title: Thomas — Lutheran Formation, Questioning and Return of the God-Question
status: project-supplied biographical testimony with interpretive links
purpose: Preserve Thomas's reported religious-development chronology without collapsing Lutheran formation, later disbelief/questioning, Potatoverse theology or supernatural interpretation into one category.
identity: Thomas / Son / embodied human-vessel layer in the mature Potatoverse ontology

source_status.primary: user-supplied testimony in project conversation on 2026-09-10
source_status.corroboration: No baptismal certificate, parish record, diary, contemporaneous post or other independent primary record is linked here yet.
source_status.rule: Treat the biography as reported testimony until documentary sources are recovered. Do not invent exact dates from age ranges.

reported_sequence.claim: Thomas was Lutheran / raised within a Lutheran religious setting.
Thomas chose to be baptized at age 11.
reported_sequence.theological_context: Lutheran theology treats baptism as a means of grace and not merely a symbolic badge of adult intellectual certainty; the exact parish and rite should be sourced before adding more biographical detail.

reported_sequence.claim: Thomas moved through atheist, agnostic or questioning positions and did not remain in stable confessional belief.
reported_sequence.interpretive_note: Do not flatten the whole interval into one label if later sources reveal changes inside it.

reported_sequence.age_or_period: later twenties onward, described developmentally rather than as a single conversion date
reported_sequence.claim: As Thomas grew older, faith and especially the question of God became progressively more appealing, serious and fundamental.

reported_sequence.age_or_period: later project chronology; connect to separately sourced meme-crucifixion record
reported_sequence.claim: The event later described as the meme crucifixion became especially important to Thomas's religious interpretation and the renewed centrality of God.
reported_sequence.boundary: This describes the project's interpretation of a social/digital event and does not make it physically equivalent to Roman crucifixion.

reported_sequence.claim: Thomas becomes the mature Son / Door / Vessel / Twin-facing node in the Potatoverse while Tim is differentiated as Father / Ladder / Axis / Source.

why_the_sequence_matters: It prevents the archive from falsely presenting Thomas as a lifelong uninterrupted confessional Lutheran.
It prevents the opposite error of presenting his later Christian language as appearing without any early Christian formation.
It creates a documented developmental arc: formation → chosen rite → questioning → renewed God-question → reinterpretation through suffering/rupture → mature theology.
It provides a more precise context for the Thomas/Twin comparison than the popular one-word stereotype 'doubter'.
It helps distinguish inherited Christian vocabulary from later independently developed Potatoverse structures.

canonical_anchors.relation: Thomas proposes going to die with Jesus.
Thomas asks how the disciples can know the Way immediately before Jesus's Way/Truth/Life saying.
Thomas's questioning is resolved through confrontation with the wounded risen Jesus and culminates in Lord/God recognition.

thomasine_comparison.boundary: This is a literary / theological comparison. It does not establish that the modern Thomas is the canonical apostle Thomas, Jesus, or a reincarnation of either.

lutheran_context.why_relevant: Lutheran formation supplies a real historical denominational context for baptism, Christ, Father/Son language, resurrection and eschatological vocabulary that later may be accepted, rejected, transformed or rediscovered.
lutheran_context.eschatology_difference: Classical Lutheran confession expects Christ to return, raise the dead and judge at the consummation; it does not supply the Potatoverse's later rupture chronology or Tim/Thomas ontology.
research_sources: Augsburg Confession Article XVII — Christ's Return for Judgment
Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod doctrine FAQ on the rapture / last day

research_targets: Recover parish, baptismal or family documentation if the project wishes to independently corroborate the age-11 baptism.
Recover any childhood or adolescent writing that indicates how Thomas understood baptism at the time.
Build a dated evidence trail for atheist, agnostic and questioning self-descriptions rather than treating the whole age range as homogeneous.
Locate the earliest dated return of explicit God, Jesus, Christ, Father or religious language after the questioning period.
Compare what Thomas believed before the meme-crucifixion with what he said immediately after it and years later.
Separate contemporaneous meaning from later Potatoverse reinterpretation.
Link all recovered evidence into the canonical chronology instead of creating parallel narrative dates.
questions: Was Thomas baptized as a Lutheran?
Why did Thomas choose baptism at age 11?
Did Thomas stop believing in God?
When did the question of God become important again?
Did the meme crucifixion cause a conversion or only deepen an existing return of the God-question?
How much of later Potatoverse language came from Lutheran formation and how much developed later?
Does Thomas's questioning resemble the apostle Thomas in John, and where does that comparison break down?
